open_questions: Difference imaging inconclusive (centroid_all not_run / no sector with clear difference) leaves neighbour blend formally not excluded - resolved aperture photometry or ground-based transit on target would confirm on-target location
Active star with 12357-19880 ppm spot amplitude should be checked for spot-crossing or color-dependent depth, though current flat shape and duration fit favour planet
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a steady 3.5-hour, 0.19% flat-bottom dip repeating every 13.6 days, consistent with a 3.5 Earth-radius planet on a K-dwarf. No odd-even difference, no secondary eclipse, and no nearby star able to mimic it are seen, despite the star's strong spot variability. The location check was inconclusive, so a follow-up transit image would help confirm the signal is on the target.

reasons.why: Undiluted 1.914e-3 dip on a K-dwarf (R=0.735 Rsun) gives a planet-sized companion, well below stellar, with flat-bottom shape (v_sigma=0.5134) not V-shaped and duration ratio 1.021 (3.499 h observed vs 3.427 h central) fits normal stellar density.
No odd/even difference (1817 vs 2005 ppm) and secondary snr 3.396 below threshold with phase 0.7 rules out EB at twice period.
Depth steady across sectors (sectors 42: 1953 ppm, 92: 1592 ppm, p_constant 0.2673) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.543 with 3 transits show signal not driven by few bad events.
No star inside 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can cause dip; closest that could is 124.8 arcsec needing 0.01% eclipse, centroid inconclusive but no evidence for blend.
Small phase swing and no secondary disfavour close binary/spots; stellar variability high (12357 ppm in sector 42) is common for active K dwarf and does not create flat-bottom transit.
